item.title: Research trips for journalists to Africa, Asia, Latin America
item.description: Young journalists from North Rhine-Westphalia can apply for research trips to Africa, Asia, or Latin America. These trips allow them to further their education in a new environment and gain intensive and personal insights into the perspectives and behaviors of a foreign culture without time pressure.

DFRLab Digital Sherlocks
item.description:
Digital Sherlocks is a free, annual, live online training program for members of civil society, journalists, researchers and analysts who are committed to monitoring and protecting the information environment in their respective regions. 

The program spans three months, with two to three sessions per week delivered live. Participants can register for as many sessions as they would like based on interests and schedules. Given the global nature of each cohort, we schedule sessions to accommodate as many time zones as possible. 

All sessions are delivered in English. Applicants are expected to have a sufficient level of English proficiency to actively follow live training sessions and engage with written communications and materials.

The program offers over twenty specialized modules covering the “how” and “why” of open-source investigations. Sessions are primarily led by the DFRLab’s global team of experts. Early sessions introduce foundational concepts and frameworks focused on cultivating the investigative mindset and understanding online influence operations. The program progresses to more advanced topics on open-source investigative techniques, tools, and methodologies. 

Deadline: 2026-05-11

IPI hosts virtual newsroom visit [Worldwide]
item.description:
Journalists can register for this free virtual event.

The International Press Institute’s (IPI) Local News and Innovation Network is hosting a virtual newsroom visit to Liceulice, a monthly Serbian street paper that is dedicated to strengthening civic activism, solidarity and emancipation. 

During the newsroom visit, Liceulice’s team will provide provide insight into what it's like to run a print paper in the age of digitalization, the future of print publications and more. 

The visit will take place on Oct. 15 via Zoom.

Registration is ongoing.
